beats.care: Stuck at Panjagutta or Gachibowli daily? This is about how your commute gets fixed for the next 10 years.
beats.what: An online petition to the Governor, CM and officials asks to review flyover and road-widening projects.
beats.why: Petitioners say adding roads only invites more private vehicles and doesn't keep traffic moving for long.

cards.body: They want an audit of flyovers, public cost-benefit and air-quality studies before new projects, new buses, bus-priority lanes, more frequent Metro trains, and feeder buses to Metro and MMTS stations.
Planners call it 'induced demand': when roads get easier, more people drive, and jams return.
cards.title: why don't more roads fix traffic?

a.body: Move people, not vehicles. Fund buses, Metro, walking and cycling first.
a.label: Petitioners say

b.body: Ease junction bottlenecks quickly through programmes like SRDP and HCITI.
b.label: Road projects aim to

opts: Pause flyovers, invest in public transport
cards.q: What do the petitioners mainly want?
cards.why: They argue road expansion fails and public transport, walking and cycling should come first.

hook: More flyovers or more buses? Planners say *stop building roads*

learn.t: 'Induced demand' means building more road space often leads to more traffic, not less.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: Online petition urges govt. to 'unchoke' Hyderabad roads (print, Hyderabad edition, 24 Oct, p.2)

tldr: Urban planners and citizens petitioned the government to pause new flyovers and road widening and invest in buses, Metro and walking.
watch: Watch whether the government reviews SRDP and HCITI projects or responds to the petition.
